title: Dot product, angle, and orthogonality
section: Analytic Geometry of R3 ▷ The Dot Product
terms: dot product; scalar product; angle between vectors; orthogonal vectors; perpendicular vectors.

The identity ∥u ± v∥ = ∥u∥ + ∥v∥ ± 2u · v often replaces coordinate calculations. Cauchy–
Schwarz, |u·v| ≤ ∥u∥∥v∥, bounds angles and linear expressions, with equality precisely for linearly
dependent vectors. Dot products are distributive over addition; this is not an associativity law
for a product of three vectors.

question.text:
3
Vectors u, v, w ∈ R satisfy u = v + w, u · v = 0, and u · w = 0. Which conclusion must hold?
(A) v = w = 0
(B) v · w = 0
(C) u = 0 and v = −w
(D) u, v, w are three nonzero mutually perpendicular vectors.
(E) The angle between u and v is π/2.

solution.text:
Bilinearity gives u · u = u · (v + w) = 0. Positive definiteness of the Euclidean norm forces
u = 0, so v = −w. They need not vanish individually. A zero dot product with a zero vec-
tor does not define an angle, so the last assertion is not valid.
